reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous pattern recognition with external XAI tools to systematically identify shared spurious features. This ensures both high-level intuition and quantitative attribution scores are leveraged to detect features that appear consistently across misclassified instances and have high model importance despite lacking semantic relevance. The combination increases confidence in identifying spurious correlations that might be missed by either method alone.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are common across all three misclassified instances (13590, 2021, 14962) and note their values.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features and their values in all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature (e.g., marital-status=Married-civ-spouse, occupation=Sales, etc.) is semantically meaningful or likely to be correlated with income in a spurious way (e.g., due to dataset bias or co-occurrence with other features).
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A qualitative assessment of semantic relevance and potential for spurious correlation

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides robust, consistent feature importance scores across instances, allowing us to detect which features have high attribution in misclassified predictions. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local interpretability to validate attribution, while sensitivity analysis helps confirm whether setting a feature to zero significantly alters the prediction—indicating its spurious influence. Using intersection-based comparison ensures only features present in all misclassified cases are considered, filtering out noise and focusing on genuine shared spurious signals.
